verses.text: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Lebanon’s glory will be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see Yahweh’s glory, the excellence of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong. Don’t be afraid. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. Grass with reeds and rushes will be in the habitation of jackals, where they lay.
A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools will not go there.
No lion will be there, nor will any ravenous animal go up on it. They will not be found there; but the redeemed will walk there.
The Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”

footnotes.content: The wasteland will bloom—not because it earned it, but because God's goodness reaches even the forgotten places. When you feel parched and small, remember: the same power that turns wilderness to roses is turned toward you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sharon, Carmel—real places of beauty—are what Isaiah names as the standard for this desert's transformation. He's saying: even the most fruitful lands in Israel will pale beside what God is making here. The glory isn't borrowed; it's surpassing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Weak hands. Feeble knees. Isaiah sees us—not as we wish to be seen, but as we actually are. And he doesn't tell us to try harder; he tells us to be strengthened. The work is not yours to do alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear whispers that God has forgotten your cause. But Isaiah says: behold, He comes with vengeance—not against you, but FOR you. His retribution is on your behalf. Let that word settle: you are vindicated in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blind eyes opened, deaf ears unstopped. These aren't only about physical sight and sound—they're about finally perceiving God's nearness, finally hearing His voice after a long silence. The redemption is intimacy restored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lame leaping, the mute singing—joy that moves and finds voice. And the wilderness springs forth water: life returning where death ruled. Isaiah shows us people and place transformed together, as if creation itself is dancing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The jackals' haunts—places of danger and desolation—become pools and grass. Isaiah names the specific wasteland to show: nowhere is beyond God's reach. Even where the wild things nested, there is now rest and plenty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A highway called The Holy Way—a path so clear that even the foolish cannot miss it, yet so consecrated that the unclean will not tread it. This is the road home, and it's marked for those who choose to walk in it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No lions, no ravenous beasts—not because danger vanishes from creation, but because the redeemed walk in a protection that silences every threat. You are safe, not because the world is harmless, but because you belong to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: the ransomed ones returning with singing, sorrow and sighing fled away. Centuries on, we recognize this homecoming—not yet complete, yet already begun in Christ. Every grief He carries is one that will not follow us home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
